scenario.note: A global upper limit on total output is introduced across all industries and years. The plan will adjust production levels to respect this bound while maintaining feasibility and maximizing employment.
The input per unit of output for steel using steel is changed directly in the input_output table.
The minimum capacity built is quantified as the total extra capacity built in year 5, summed over all industries.
A cap on total extra capacity built over the planning horizon is introduced as a linear constraint on the sum of capacity built per year.
The floor on output is applied to transport industry production, setting a minimum total output of 1110 million USD.
The input per unit of output for transport using transport is changed from the original value to 0.5, reducing the self-supply requirement of transport.
A floor on the capacity built is modeled as an upper bound on the total extra capacity built over the planning horizon.
A minimum output requirement is imposed per industry, with a baseline of 100 million USD per year.
A cap on total capacity built over the planning horizon is added as a linear constraint on the sum of extra_capacity across years.
A change in exogenous consumption demand is modeled by setting the external_demand column in the industries table for a specific industry.
The initial productive capacity for steel is changed to 400 million USD/year to assess its impact on the economic plan.

The manpower per unit of capacity built is scaled uniformly across all industries. Since no specific values are given, a neutral scaling (factor 1.0) is applied to maintain consistency with the original model unless a specific shift is provided.

A minimum stock requirement is added across all years and industries, ensuring non-negative stock levels.

The input per unit of output for steel to coal is set to 0.15, representing a change in the input-output coefficient for one row in the input-output table.
A cap is placed on the total stock held across all years, with a limit of 100 million USD. The scope covers years 1 to 5, as year 6 is the steady state and stock is not defined there.

A cap is placed on the total stock held in each year from year 1 to 5, limiting it to 100 million USD.
